R301 — XeStrata xe0.1.42 evaluation and coverage
Date: 2026-10-12 (Asia/Tokyo)
Scope: read-only review of pristine XeStrata xe0.1.42 (da3d426079019daa6e01388d03b0d94ae67070b7), current integrated Strata source (9b03…; engine/build/setup files equivalent to the already measured source), and retained public benchmark summaries and audits. No source/test/controller edit, import, build, GPU/model/service operation, cleanup, or Git mutation was performed. This report records evaluation eligibility; it does not authorize or claim a new run.

Decision

The Xe0.1.42 source is useful as a candidate/reference implementation, but retained evidence does not qualify it as a safe or optimized replacement for current B570 Strata. One pristine-source 32K diagnostic exists. It is a single non-controlled sample; there is no matched clean 32K/64K timing and math comparison against the current integrated engine, nor a corrected-Xe long-context completion. No CPU or SYCL candidate in the later Xe tip delta merits promotion on current evidence. Keep current measured tuning as a separate binary/source result and do not attribute its gains to Xe0.1.42 or the latest server merge.

Pristine-source evidence and performance boundary

The latest remote check still resolves official v0.1.43 to 7695859 and XeStrata xe0.1.42 to da3d426; the 2026-10-12 consolidated update reports no newer inference source. Its 32K Xe row is one diagnostic: 217.61 prefill and 10.41 decode tokens/s, LLVM 7.1.1 free build, batched8192 label, 29/144 cache slots filled. Full argv/environment and all effective controls are not available in that summary. The official v0.1.43 cache128 and cache512 rows are separate single diagnostics at 19.07/6.29 and 17.77/8.48 tokens/s, respectively, but use serial verify windows, tracing/validation instrumentation, and a different compiler. They are not a speed ranking against Xe.

The selected integrated 32K recipe records 376.42 prefill and 8.27 decode tokens/s across three clean native-dequant-batched samples. It is a separately identified binary/source. It is not a matched Xe comparison and its difference cannot be assigned to the current source merge. The 2026-10-12 server completion and consolidated update add Python/API changes only; engine/build/setup sources are byte-identical to the previously measured engine branch, and no model/GPU inference was run for that merge. Therefore these updates provide no fresh Xe performance or engine safety evidence.

Older published Xe release measurements (Xe0.1.40.2.1 versus upstream v0.1.41) show useful multi-device candidate performance on B70, RTX 4070 and RX 9060 XT, but they are two-run medians for an older Xe revision, compiler/path setup and benchmark protocol. They do not establish xe0.1.42 behavior or current B570 adoption.

Safety and architecture interpretation

XeStrata has hardware-specific Xe2/XMX, joint_matrix and DP4a routes. Xe2 XMX code is not directly applicable to NVIDIA B570; portable joint_matrix/CUDA-target routes require confirming actual target selection and capability. Existing Xe source audits identify plausible prompt GEMM, fused GDN, QSA prompt-attention, MoE dispatch and AVX2 CPU implementations, but candidate presence is not B570 validation. The historical Xe safety audit records a 39bd binary mismatch/fault and a distinct corrected 8K diagnostic; the corrected 8K record explicitly does not qualify 32K/64K, math equivalence, quality, or full context. Do not transfer the earlier failure to the corrected binary or promote the short diagnostic into a long pass.

The newer Xe mainline delta audit found no changes to native_expert.cpp or IQ AVX2 kernels in its examined range. Its doorbell system-fence/store change has a B70 microbenchmark result only; it has no B570 end-to-end decode result, and the standalone probe is not identical to the production helper. Its ShortReadCost policy chooses a path for short fresh text in serving; it is not a batched long-prefill GEMM optimization. Neither finding supports an Xe0.1.42 CPU speedup claim.

The corrected Xe 8K diagnostic indicates explicit host-USM and issuer-off settings and reports 144 physical cache slots for requested budget 128. Historical 29/144 fill belongs to the older host-USM source and must not be assumed for the corrected executable. Requested cache and ring values do not establish actual occupancy/effective behavior; prior source review notes Xe’s effective ring can differ from a baseline despite the same requested ring. Treat execution controls, allocator, issuer, cache fill, and ring as explicit whole-engine comparison conditions.

Long-context coverage status

There is no matched, clean, repeated, corrected-Xe 32K or 64K comparison. The existing corrected Xe receipt is only an 8,193-token/two-chunk diagnostic, with one generated token; its record sets performance_eligible=false, math_equivalence=false, quality_qualified=false and full262144_qualified=false. It establishes only that specific short diagnostic closed without a new fault under its recorded conditions.

Historical baseline evidence is also bounded: a 64K baseline timing sample completed prefill but stopped after three generated tokens, so it cannot support a 64-token decode comparison. Existing baseline 32K execution/math admission is not a matched timing row. No 262,144-token input, RESTORE lifecycle, full-context math or quality result is established by READY capacity, a shorter prompt, or LP5 observations.

Recommended evaluation boundary

If Main elects to continue, use the recorded corrected-Xe comparison contract rather than reusing the older pristine-Xe controller. First close exact build/link identity and source/executable hashes, then establish fresh long-geometry safety/fault admission with actual environment and effective settings. Keep a fresh 32K control or 64K trial paired with the same baseline source/binary, fixture, chunk, request shape and runtime conditions. Record cache fill/effective ring, prompt progress and timer boundaries separately. Require at least three fresh alternating runs per arm for an initial timing comparison; count decode only when all 64 generated tokens complete with length. Maintain a separate math/quality gate: timing, finite output and LP5 are not proof of state/full-logit/quality equivalence. Do not infer 262K input or RESTORE qualification from 32K/64K execution.

Reviewed retained evidence: R286 parameter qualification and latest pristine measurements; R288 candidate/B570 and FP32 audit; R330 corrected-Xe long comparison contract; R338 Xe latest-tip performance/build delta; R347 verifier/lifetime review; R368 minimal source-built LLVM GPU selection review; consolidated latest-update and v0.1.43 server-completion reports; Xe0.1.40.2.1 release table. These are source/report reviews only; no new measurements were generated.
